question: Shared: progression from MCI to AD within 36 months (pMCI vs sMCI) in ADNI1/ADNI2. P-23's model is multimodal (sMRI + FDG-PET + CSF); P-3 uses baseline structural MRI only. The shared channel is MRI, so condition 1 holds under the multimodal clause, with the added PET and CSF recorded as a candidate explanation.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (match); both papers also give AUC.

figures.P-23: Tri-modal TASNet (A0) 85.00% = 17/20 on the single held-out test split (8:1:1 of 200 MCI; SEN 83.33 = 10/12 pMCI, SPE 87.50 = 7/8 sMCI). No interval is reported. Wilson with n = 20: z^2/n = 0.19207; centre = (0.85 + 0.09604)/1.19207 = 0.7936; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.85*0.15/20 + 3.8415/1600)/1.19207 = 0.1540; interval [0.640, 0.948]. AUC 0.9167: Hanley-McNeil with 12 pMCI/8 sMCI gives SE 0.0643, interval [0.791, 1.000]. Matched sMRI-only ablation (Table 6, A1): 65.00% = 13/20 (SEN 8/12, SPE 5/8), Wilson [0.433, 0.819]; AUC 0.6667, Hanley-McNeil SE 0.1231, interval [0.425, 0.908].
figures.P-3: CAAT ensemble, baseline sMRI only: 74.61% (variance 0.002), 5-fold CV over 593 MCI (295 pMCI, 298 sMCI). No interval is reported. Wilson with n = 593: z^2/n = 0.00648; centre = (0.7461 + 0.00324)/1.00648 = 0.7445; half-width = 0.0350; interval [0.710, 0.780]. AUC 0.780: Hanley-McNeil with 295/298 gives SE 0.0190, interval [0.743, 0.817].

matched_figure_check: P-23 reports its own model under P-3's condition, the sMRI-only ablation in Table 6 (A1): 65.00% (13/20, Wilson [0.433, 0.819]), AUC 0.667. That lies below P-3's 74.61%, not above it. P-3's 74.61% falls inside the A1 interval, and the two-proportion z is -0.89. A1's point estimate lies outside P-3's narrow interval, but in the opposite direction to the recorded disagreement and on 20 test subjects. The ablation shows that the recorded gap (85.00 against 74.61) comes from adding FDG-PET and CSF (A1 65.00 -> A0 85.00). A paper thus shows the modality difference is sufficient to produce the gap, so the pair fails condition 3.
performance_validity: Not excluded. P-23's 85.00% accuracy and AUC 0.9167 are below 0.97, although the test split is only 20 subjects. P-3's 74.61% is well below.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input modalities: sMRI + FDG-PET + CSF (P-23) against sMRI only (P-3). SHOWN SUFFICIENT by P-23's own ablation (sMRI only 65.00%, tri-modal 85.00%), hence the condition-3 failure.
candidate_explanations.quote: The substantial improvement to 85.00% (A0) demonstrates that sMRI, PET, and CSF are mutually reinforcing.

candidate_explanations.difference: Evaluation-set size and design: one 20-subject held-out split (P-23) against 5-fold CV over 593 (P-3).
candidate_explanations.quote: was stratified into training, validation, and test sets (8:1:1)

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort selection: P-23 requires baseline FDG-PET and CSF (200 MCI), while P-3 uses the Wen et al. split of 593 MCI.
candidate_explanations.quote: with baseline T1-weighted sMRI, FDG-PET, and CSF biomarkers (Abeta42, TAU, PTAU)

reason: The two papers share a clinical question (36-month pMCI vs sMCI in ADNI) and a metric. Under the literal wording of condition 4, P-23's 85.00% lies outside P-3's Wilson interval [0.710, 0.780], although P-3's 74.61% lies inside P-23's [0.640, 0.948] and the two-proportion z is only 1.27. The pair fails condition 3. P-23 reports its model on P-3's input (sMRI only) at 65.00%, below P-3, and its ablation attributes the whole recorded gap to the added PET and CSF inputs. The papers' own data therefore account for the difference.
